picks.thesis: Convergence. Three House filers bought TSM between 2026-01-08 and 2026-05-08 across six disclosures, all in the $1,001-$15,000 band, with lags of 11-39 days. Alongside that, eleven officers filed non-10b5-1 open-market buys: Chairman and CEO Wei Che-Chia $11,402 and ten colleagues on 2026-06-05, plus VP Yuan Lipen $79,190 on 2026-06-22, each disclosed within 1-4 days. The Form 4 leg is broad and promptly filed, but the individual amounts are small for officers of this rank, and every buy predates the drawdown: last close 374.67 is the 90-day low, -11.05% over five days and -17.67% over thirty.
key_risks: The 2026-06-05 insider buys are uniform in date and small in size ($3,040-$11,402), a pattern that may reflect routine compensation-linked activity rather than discretionary conviction; the data does not say which.
All evidence predates the price action: TSM's last close is its own 90-day low, so the buyers are underwater on the disclosed dates.
Congressional amounts are $1,001-$15,000 bands only - the true sizes are unknown and could be trivial.
The congressional leg is 3-7 months stale by as_of.
picks.invalidation: Officers who bought on 2026-06-05 and 2026-06-22 begin filing sales, or no further insider buying appears while the price continues to set new lows below 374.67.
